findings.what: Invocation-wide gate decisions can bypass both required human turn boundaries.
findings.why: run_workflow normalizes every supplied input once and carries the same gate_a/gate_b keys through every freshly resolved phase. A decision supplied before its gate is reached therefore becomes immediately consumable after P3 or P6 instead of ending the turn at Gate A or Gate B; the resolver probe returned ready P4 and P7 owners for those carried keys.

findings.what: The resolver treats presence-only, incomplete phase inputs as ready and can spend attempts before boundary validation.
findings.why: _REQUIRED_INPUTS omits the timezone-aware now value required by P1-P4 and tests only whether gate_a/gate_b top-level names exist. Missing now or incomplete gate mappings consequently resolve ready and fail later inside an attempt, contradicting the complete missing-input/human-decision contract and the rule that human stops consume no attempt.

findings.what: The attempt utility does not provide atomic phase staging; deterministic owners write directly into the live case.
findings.why: _run_handler discards _attempt_dir, and _register_sources promotes each request inside its loop. If a later source is invalid, the attempt fails and retries while earlier source bytes, receipts, and catalogue records remain live. The supplied gated-hash probe ended P1 unavailable after three attempts with the first source already present, violating AC3 atomic promotion.

findings.what: README projection deletes journalist-authored content that exactly matches the legacy Outputs block.
findings.why: After removing the marked Anomaly-owned block, project_readme globally replaces every exact _OUTPUTS occurrence. An unmarked journalist-authored Outputs section is therefore erased; the pure replacement probe preserved only the later Notes section.

findings.what: Public resume, inspect, and direct writer paths do not enforce the required whole-case no-symlink scan.
findings.why: resume_case and inspect_case load selected files without _scan_case_tree, and public domain writers such as register_local_source rely on resume_case. A nested in-case symlink is accepted; in source registration, a destination symlink resolving to another in-case artifact can be followed and overwritten. Only run_workflow and fork_case currently scan the whole tree.

findings.what: The multi-phase loop does not recheck whole-case containment after dynamic reasoning owners mutate the case.
findings.why: run_workflow scans once before entering the loop. P5/P6 invoke external adapters that write case artifacts, then the next iteration loads state and executes another owner without rescanning. A symlink introduced by an invoked owner can therefore reach later public reads or writes in the same call, contrary to AC7's every-path preflight.

findings.what: Canonical-equivalent Unicode identities bypass reviewer independence at both gates.
findings.why: The Gate A/reviewer and reviewer/Gate B checks compare casefold values only. Composed 'Réviewer' and decomposed 'Réviewer' compare unequal by casefold but equal under the project's canonical_key, so one logical identity can occupy separated roles.

findings.what: A completed snapshot with missing authoritative identities is trusted as P7-complete.
findings.why: changed_identities iterates only identity keys already recorded; a missing or malformed identities map becomes an empty mapping and yields no invalidation. A sequential completed map through P7 is then accepted without checking source, detector, gate, draft, replay, review, or Gate B artifacts; the pure probe reported completed P7 with identity_change None.

findings.what: The retained retry tests no longer verify credential-redacted durable failure evidence.
findings.why: The current test asserts three attempts and relative attempt paths but injects no credential and inspects neither failure.json, event error fields, state failures, nor blocked_reason. The deleted WorkflowRunner test was the only redaction assertion. AC3's durable failure evidence is consumer-observable, so the plan's ambiguous reuse/delete claim is dominated by reuse but is not valid: a focused public replacement test is owed.

findings.what: Deleting the invalidation matrix left most authoritative identity classes without earliest-suffix coverage.
findings.why: Current public tests cover source/P1, prepared/P2, and Gate B/P7, but production still maps recommendation/P3, Gate A and detector/P4, draft/P5, and replay/review/P6. Deleting their behavioral assertions without deleting those behaviors violates the remove rule; focused state/resolution tests must replace the synthetic runner composition.

findings.what: No public test proves that future Gate A or Gate B decisions cannot cross a turn.
findings.why: The demo deliberately supplies each human decision only on a later invocation, so it cannot fail when run_workflow incorrectly carries a pre-supplied future decision through the resolver loop. The exact gate-turn behavior is consumer-observable and explicitly required by AC4.

findings.what: README preservation coverage omits completed restart and failed recomputation transitions.
findings.why: The journalist notes fixture is added immediately before Gate B invalidation and covers invalidation plus recompletion, while the chart-failure test contains no journalist-authored content. The plan explicitly claims preservation across completed restart and failure too, and those observable lifecycle cases remain unproved.

findings.what: The Markdown inertness test does not contain a standalone bare URL.
findings.why: Both URL occurrences are embedded inside Markdown-link and HTML-image syntax. The assertion that the raw URL substring disappears therefore does not exercise AC6's specifically named bare HTTP(S) autolink boundary; add prose containing a standalone URL and assert it remains visible but non-linking.
